title: Degree-zero cochains are invariants
statement: Let $G$ be a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected topological group, $A$ a finite ring, and $\mathcal C$ the abelian category of left $A$-modules with $A$-linear $G$-action and open stabilizers [lem-exc-discrete-modules-abelian]. Let $F:\mathcal C\to\operatorname{CochainComplex}(A\text{-Mod},\mathbb N)$ have termwise linear equivalences $F(M)^n\simeq\operatorname{Cont}(G^n,M)$, natural by postcomposition, and differentials $d^0m(g)=gm-m$ and $d^nf(g_1,\ldots,g_{n+1})=g_1f(g_2,\ldots,g_{n+1})+\sum_{j=1}^n(-1)^jf(g_1,\ldots,g_jg_{j+1},\ldots,g_{n+1})+(-1)^{n+1}f(g_1,\ldots,g_n)$. There exists an additive functor $V:\mathcal C\to A\text{-Mod}$ preserving finite limits, with natural linear equivalences $V(M)\simeq\bigcap_{g\in G}\ker(\rho_M(g)-1)$ whose maps are restrictions of the coefficient maps. The degree-zero homology functor of $F$ is naturally isomorphic to $V$.

proof.text: Define S(M) as the intersection of kernels of rho(g)-id, and V(M) as the module S(M). Membership is equivalent to rho(g)x=x for every g. Equivariance sends S(M) into S(N), so restrict each coefficient map to these submodules. Identity and composition hold pointwise, and the required equivalence V(M) to S(M) is the identity.

Use the abelian structure fixed in the statement by [lem-exc-discrete-modules-abelian]. Give an ordinary A-module its trivial G-action; its stabilizers are all of G, hence open. Equivariant maps from that trivial representation to M are naturally exactly A-linear maps into S(M), by the invariant-element criterion. These explicit mutually inverse hom-set maps give an adjunction L adjoint to V using Adjunction.mkOfHomEquiv. A right adjoint preserves limits; Functor.additive_of_preserves_binary_products gives additivity for the preadditive structure fixed by the statement. This works over an arbitrary ring A and does not use a commutativity hypothesis.

The set Fin 0 to G is a singleton, so all its arguments agree. Specialize the differential formula at n=0 and simplify the sum over Fin 1: d(x)(g)=rho(g)(e(x)(z))-e(x)(z). A constant cochain on an invariant element therefore lifts to cycles. Conversely, evaluate the image of a cycle under iCycles at z; the cycle equation and the differential formula prove its value invariant. Both maps are A-linear. Cancelling the monic iCycles and evaluating continuous maps pointwise prove the two inverse identities. Compose this cycles isomorphism with the inverse of CochainComplex.isoHomologyπ₀, since there is no incoming boundary in degree zero. Finally CochainComplex.isoHomologyπ₀_inv_naturality, HomologicalComplex.cyclesMap_i, and the assumed coefficient formula prove naturality, yielding the asserted natural isomorphism.
